First, notice that

$$
{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of $C:$

$$
C={{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt[18]{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt[36]{3}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Since $C=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${C}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{C}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{36} & =P{D}^{36}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt[18]{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt[36]{3}\end{aligned}]}^{36}(\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}(\sqrt[18]{3})^{36} & 0 \\ 0 & (\sqrt[36]{3})^{36}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & {3}^{1}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}27 & -3 \\ -27 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}15 & 6 \\ -12 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
